transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-10-14
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~54 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam Ortiz (Redwood SE), Noah Patel (Redwood Solutions), Priya Raman (Verdant, Head of ML), Carlos Mendes (Verdant CTO), Aisha Khan (Verdant Infra), Evan Lee (Verdant Product)

Auto-summary (auto gen, may be rough):
Verdant is evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs private for cost/unit economics. Primary concerns: per-token unit cost, latency SLOs (~100-200ms), and staying within a $10k-25k/month inference budget for POC. Discussed batching, KV/prefix caching, quantization tradeoffs and potential dedicated reserved capacity options. Next steps: pricing sheet, security docs, run benchmark.

Topics: pricing, batching, caching, dedicated capacity, latency, budget, security compliance, benchmark

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: hey everyone thanks for carving out time, um quick intros, i'll kick it off. i'm maya from redwood, ae on this account.
[00:06] Priya: hi thanks, priya here, head of ml at verdant. carlos and aisha on as well.
[00:10] Carlos: hey, good to meet you.
[00:12] Liam: liam, se for redwood — i'll drive the tech details. quick agenda, cost focus first then architecture options, then next steps.
[00:20] Aisha: good, we care about cost/unit mainly. we run a ton of document summarization and downstream scoring, token volumes are large.
[00:27] Evan: yeah budget for initial POC is basically 10k a month but if perf looks good we can scale to 25k.

[00:35] Liam: understood. can you share current stack? like are you on any hosted apis now? typical model sizes?
[00:40] Priya: we use a mix — some open models self-hosted, some calls to openai for chat tasks. sequence lengths vary, average prompt+resp about 800 tokens, peak 2k. throughput target is ~50 qps during business hours.
[00:55] Maya: that helps. two levers to control unit cost we usually discuss: batching and caching. batching improves TPU/GPU utilization but adds latency; caching (prefix / KV) reduces repeated work for similar prompts. also quantized model variants can drop per-token GPU cost.
[01:10] Priya: can you give concrete numbers? like hosted per-token vs dedicated unit costs, examples?
[01:14] Liam: sure. rough headline for hosted: our managed hosted pricing is X cents per 1k tokens for smaller context workloads — sorry i'm trying to avoid quoting an exact public number on this call, but we sent a pricing deck — for a POC we normally model two scenarios: hosted per-token (no infra overhead) and dedicated reserved capacity (capacity commit).
[01:30] Carlos: right but what's the delta? we need to know at what volume dedicated becomes cheaper.
[01:34] Liam: totally. for example, on dedicated a 4-GPU pool running quantized Llama-derivative can bring token cost down ~2.5-4x versus peaks on hosted per-token at high sustained throughput (this includes amortized infra + ops). the break-even depends on utilization; at 50 qps and average 800 tokens the dedicated starts to make sense around the high end of your budget — so if you're at 25k/mo sustained, dedicated looks compelling.
[01:54] Priya: okay but does that assume perfect batching? we have low latency SLOs, like 150ms median.
[02:00] Liam: good callout — batching increases throughput but can bump tail latency. our runtime supports smart batching with latency-aware policies; you can cap batch window to keep median under 150ms and still get decent batching for smaller sequences. also prefix/KV cache often knocks down work for repeated system prompts or doc prefixes — that can reduce effective token cost independent of batching.
[02:20] Aisha: how do we estimate cost savings from KV cache? our workflows have many similar seeds.
[02:24] Liam: you can model cache hit-rate. if you get say 30-40% hit rate on KV cache for doc prefixes, that directly reduces token compute for those hits — so roughly 30% fewer generated tokens needing full attention per request. combined with batching, your effective p50 token cost drops multiplicatively.
[02:41] Priya: hmm the math is a bit hand-wavy. can you show a sample calc?
[02:44] Maya: yes we will send an example. quick off the cuff: suppose hosted is 1.0 unit per generated token; with 30% cache hit and batching savings of 20% effective compute, your effective cost could be 1.0 * (1 - 0.3) * 0.8 = 0.56 units per token on average. on dedicated, per-token compute might be 0.3-0.5 units because of quantization and cheaper GPU amortization.
[03:05] Carlos: so in that example dedicated ends up ~2x cheaper. but we need to factor operational overhead and commitments. what's the commit term?
[03:13] Maya: dedicated reserves are monthly or annual — monthly commitments exist but annual gives better pricing. also we offer burst capacity on top to handle spikes.
[03:20] Evan: for POC we want no long-term lock, ideally monthly or trial credits.
[03:24] Maya: we can structure a 30-day dedicated trial with an evaluated commit. we'll send options.

[03:30] Liam: also worth flagging private deployment (VPC / on-prem) — that adds infra cost and ops but addresses data residency and full control. usually more expensive than dedicated because of customer-managed infra.
[03:41] Priya: security is important — SOC2 and ISO are musts, and audit logs. can you host KMS/HSM?
[03:47] Maya: yes we support KMS integration for hosted and dedicated and HSM for private deployments; SOC2+/ISO docs we'll attach.

[03:55] Aisha: back to performance — we need 95th < 300ms ideally. will batching break that?
[04:00] Liam: the runtime's latency aware batching tries to keep p95 bounds; we can set per-route policies: small batch windows for low-latency routes, larger windows for high-throughput offline scoring. also model selection matters — smaller quantized models hit latency targets easier.
[04:16] Priya: do you have any benchmark artifacts we can run against?
[04:19] Liam: yes, we have a benchmark runbook and sample workloads. proposal: run a 24h benchmark using your dataset with a 2k context on both hosted and dedicated trial to capture costs and p95/p50. we'll instrument token-level cost and KV hit rates.
[04:33] Carlos: sounds good. what about tooling for cost visibility?
[04:36] Maya: console has token-level breakdown, per-route dashboards, and cost allocation by tag so you can map to product teams.

[04:43] Evan: on pricing specifics — will you share a spreadsheet with modeled scenarios?
[04:47] Maya: yes i'll attach a hosted vs dedicated spreadsheet with line items: per-token, infra amort, cache assumptions, batch windows, and example monthly cost for 10k, 25k budgets.

[04:57] Priya: one more question — how do rollouts and fallback work? we may want canary to hosted if dedicated capacity is full.
[05:03] Liam: supported — smart routing can fallback to hosted or smaller model variants. you can configure policy by route, latency, or cost.

[05:10] Priya: perfect.
[05:12] Maya: recap and next steps: i'll send pricing sheet and security docs by tomorrow, liam will propose the benchmark config and runbook, priya will provision dataset and keys for the trial, and we'll meet week of 2026-10-27 to review.
[05:24] Carlos: ok thanks all.
[05:26] Maya: thanks everyone. bye.

End of transcript.

Call notes (auto):
- Customer objective: pick lowest total cost that meets latency and compliance (POC budget $10k/mo, scale target $25k).
- Technical constraints: average 800 tokens, peaks 2k, target 50 qps, p95 < 300ms.
- Economics levers discussed: batching windows, KV/prefix cache hit rates, quantized model variants, dedicated reserved capacity vs hosted per-token.
- Risks: KV hit rate uncertainty, commit size for dedicated, tail latency under batching.
- Agreed next steps: pricing sheet, security docs, 24h benchmark on dedicated trial and hosted baseline.
